newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM gold ends mixed,gains pared on yen's rebound.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM gold ends mixed,gains pared on yen's rebound.

text.p: Tokyo gold futures ended narrowly mixed on Tuesday after early gains were pared after the yen rebounded against the dollar, traders said.
Gold prices ranged from three yen per gram lower to three firmer, with benchmark April finishing up two yen at 1,385 yen.
News of discrepancies over estimates of Bre-X Mineral Services Ltd's Busang deposit had little impact on the Tokyo gold market, traders said.
Bullion was quoted firmer at $343.10/50 per ounce at 0727 GMT, against $342.50/343.00 in New York on Monday.

In the gold futures market, private investors took profits from the outset, based on a view that the dollar's gains have now stalled. Trade houses bought futures and sold spot gold in arbitrage dealings for most of the day, traders said.
"Despite selling by trade houses, the bullion market was resilient as overseas investors tended to take a moderately bullish stance toward bullion," one trader said.
"Buying below $343 by overseas investors could support the market," he said.
Platinum futures were mostly weaker, while palladium futures were mixed in directionless trade.
"In palladium futures, most investors were sidelined, waiting for news as to when Russia will resume exports of the metal," one trader said.

Palladium short-term lease rates remained at high levels, partly due to a large overhang of short positions held by private investors in TOCOM futures. Prices ranged from three yen per gram weaker to six firmer, with benchmark April down three at 604 yen. Benchmark April platinum was down four yen at 1,472 yen. Silver futures were mixed. Benchmark April closed 0.2 yen per 10 grams weaker at 195.7 yen.
